Use a machine address on your Tailscale network and a valid SSH account and port. Public, local and mixed DNS routes are refused.

The private host operation could not finish. Check the phone’s Linux setup and private network, then retry.

Connect both devices to your Tailscale. These checks show status and addresses; they do not prove VPN membership. DNS is resolved once, every answer must be in the tailnet ranges, and SSH uses the validated numeric address with a pinned key.

Use a separate Ubuntu 24.04 account without root access. Check these tools first. Setup checks the system, nonroot UID, architecture, Python and user service manager; it does not install packages with sudo.

Keep a rescue session open. Replace MACHINE_TAILSCALE_IP with the actual numeric address and remove public or wildcard ListenAddress entries. These owner commands change the whole SSH daemon. The installer only reads actual listening sockets on the selected SSH port and refuses public, wildcard or ordinary LAN listeners; it does not change the firewall or SSH bindings. Verify every other SSH port separately.
Run the first command once with administrator access. The installer reads Linger and requires yes, then checks that systemctl --user works. It never enables linger itself or requests a sudo password.

Keep an administrator session open. Replace PHONE_TAILSCALE_IP and MACHINE_TAILSCALE_IP with the actual numeric addresses. Validate before reload. Earlier SSH directives may override this file. The installer checks local TCP forwarding, disabled reverse and socket forwarding, no tunnel devices, UseDNS no, DisableForwarding no, public-key login and the standard authorized_keys path. Parsing settings does not prove the running daemon loaded them; verify the reload yourself.
Compare this output with the app in an independent machine session before trusting it. The app computes the Ed25519 SHA256 fingerprint and blocks later identity changes.
